assertions.text: The impact of the break on the work-optional date is stated as a range or under more than one named scenario, not as a single revised date.
assertions.evidence: Headline table: "No break, stay at $196k | **2035** | 2032 – 2040" and "Break, back at $150k | **2039** | 2033 – 2047"; plus multi-scenario rows (3.5%/3.0%/2.5% real: medians 2040/2041/2041) and re-entry variants ($130k → 2040, 18 months late → 2041).

assertions.text: Outcomes are reported under at least two different investment-return assumptions, one materially more conservative than the base case.
assertions.evidence: Results table reports full outcomes at 4.5% base and lower returns: "4.5% | with break | 2033 | 2036 | **2039** ... 3.4%" and "2.5% | with break | 2035 | 2037 | **2041** | 2047 | 2053 | 57.0% | 7.9%", plus 3.5% and 3.0% rows.

assertions.text: Statutory or regulatory figures quoted in the document (tax brackets or deductions, contribution limits, subsidy or poverty-line thresholds, penalty rules) each carry a source and the date they were checked.
assertions.evidence: facts.md carries per-figure source + date: "2026 federal income tax… Standard deduction $16,100. Brackets: 10% to $12,400… source: https://taxfoundation.org/… checked: 2026-08-02"; same for FPL $15,960/138% $22,025, 0% LTCG $49,450, 401(k) $24,500/IRA $7,500/HSA $4,400, COBRA 18-month and 10% penalty rules.

assertions.text: The document names which accounts fund the break and in what order.
assertions.evidence: §"which accounts pay, in what order" gives an ordered table: "1 | **HYSA** | $82,315 over 24 months"; "2 | Taxable brokerage | $0 in the base case | Held in reserve"; "3 | Roth **contribution basis** ($54,000)"; "4 | Roth earnings, HSA"; "5 | **401(k)** | **never**".

assertions.text: The funding plan either avoids early-withdrawal penalties on retirement accounts or, where a penalized withdrawal is contemplated, states the penalty and tax cost explicitly.
assertions.evidence: "The whole break is funded from cash. You do not sell a single share, and you do not touch a retirement account." Plus explicit math: "Gross 401(k) withdrawal required 60,118 / 10% early-withdrawal penalty 6,012 / Federal + Colorado income tax on it 8,267 ... Total 20,680 = 45.1%".

assertions.text: Health coverage is priced for all 24 months of the break; no part of the break period is left with unpriced or unspecified coverage.
assertions.evidence: Both break years priced: "Travel medical insurance | 960 | 600 | 1,560 / US health insurance, net of subsidy | 798 | 798 | 1,596". Marketplace runs all 24 months ("Do not cancel the US marketplace plan while abroad"); COBRA's 18-month cap is priced with a 6-month marketplace remainder.

assertions.text: The document evaluates using the low-income break years for Roth conversion or capital-gains harvesting, reaching a stated recommendation (doing either, or explicitly not, with a reason).
assertions.evidence: §Q3: "Do a small conversion — about $15,000–17,000 in each break year — and stop. Do not build a ladder" (above ~$24k MAGI costs 27–34% to save 16.4% later); harvesting: "No" — it "would put you on a $10,600 out-of-pocket-max plan" in the PCT year, plus a marginal-rate table.

assertions.text: The document connects the size or source of withdrawals and conversions during the break to health-insurance subsidy eligibility (income thresholds), rather than treating the two as independent.
assertions.evidence: "Convert only enough to lift MAGI to roughly $24,000 (150% FPL)... It buys a $6,400 credit and a 94% actuarial-value plan." Plus 401(k) raid: "premium tax credit forfeited (the withdrawal puts MAGI at 4.2× FPL, over the 4.0× cliff) 6,402", and harvesting → "65,550 (over the cliff)".

assertions.text: The planning horizon extends to at least age 95.
assertions.evidence: Life table row: "work-optional → 95 | ~2039 – 2083 | Drawdown, guardrail spending". Assumption A22: "Horizon | age 95 | Maya"; sensitivity row "Horizon to 100 not 95 | 2039 | 2047". Born Feb 1988 → 2083 = age 95.

assertions.text: Downside outcomes are described in terms of what Maya would actually live on or do differently (spending level, break shortened, working longer), not solely as a portfolio survival or success percentage.
assertions.evidence: "The floor is $53,730/yr gross, which is about $41,700 of actual living after tax and health insurance — a 34% cut from the $63,000 you are planning on"; gates prescribe "Cut Phase C from 10 months to 6 and come home in March 2029" and delayed work-optional dates (2039→2044).

assertions.text: The document states at least one if-then rule with a numeric trigger and a defined checkpoint for delaying departure or cutting the break short.
assertions.evidence: "Gate 1 — 1 March 2027 … Non-retirement liquid (HYSA + brokerage) ≥ **$111,125** … Delay notice 12 months"; "Gate 4 — 1 February 2029 … Liquid assets remaining ≥ **$24,137** | Cut the break short and start work in April 2029"

assertions.text: The document shows the effect on the plan of re-entering work later than planned or at lower pay than the base assumption.
assertions.evidence: §"what if re-entry goes badly" table: "Base: back Sep 2029 at $150k | 2039 ... Back at $130k | 2040 | 2050 ... Six months late | 2039 | 2048 ... $130k AND six months late | 2040 | 2051" plus prose: "Coming back at $130,000 instead of $150,000 costs one year at the median."

assertions.text: The asset figures the document is built on agree, within rounding, with the balances in Maya's own records.
assertions.evidence: intake.md reproduces each balance exactly: "401(k) traditional, Fidelity | $412,000 … Roth IRA | $88,500, contribution basis $54,000 … brokerage | $174,200, cost basis ~$121,000 … HYSA | $46,800 … HSA | $19,300 … Total $740,800". Derived figures track (brokerage 174,200×1.045 = 182,039; HYSA 46,800×1.01+54,000 = 101,268 → liquid 283,307).

assertions.text: The document names at least one specific item for Maya to verify with a licensed professional or the relevant official body — beyond a generic advice disclaimer.
assertions.evidence: "Questions for a professional ... Take these to a fee-only advisor or a CPA" — e.g. #2 "Confirm the no-clawback protection... Cite the authority. [26 CFR 1.36B-2(b)(6)]"; #5 "Is my 2027 bonus payable if I resign on 31 July 2027? Read the plan document."
